ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, partners, and authorized signatories against the CSSF consolidated AML/CFT directives, EU financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list (for USD clearing and foreign correspondent transactions), Interpol notices, and the Luxembourg PPE/PEP administrative list maintained by the CSSF. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for politically exposed persons, high-risk third-country nationals, and cross-border luxury-goods transactions; ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds verification must follow Articles 3-2 and 4 of the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in Luxembourgish, French, German, English, or another Latin-script language. Names in non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. The legal form suffix 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' must appear in the name. Names must be distinctive, non-misleading, and not contrary to public order. The RCS accepts filings in French and German; foreign-language names require a transliteration and must not conflict with an existing Luxembourg or trademark-protected name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the RCS, the applicant may request reconsideration from the competent RCS department within 15 days. If rejection is upheld, an administrative appeal lies to the Tribunal Administratif (Administrative Court) in Luxembourg City within three months of notification, pursuant to Article 33 of the Law of 19 December 2002. A new name reservation should be filed within 5 business days of an unfavourable decision to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered only offices is legally permissible for an SCSp under the Law of 19 December 2002, provided the service provider is an approved societal de domiciliation under Article 21-1 of that Law. For an online luxury resale platform, a virtual office is administratively accepted, but the business must maintain substantive commercial substance: decision-making facilities, complete accounting records, VAT registration, a real bank or escrow account, and appropriate compliance personnel. A pure virtual office without employee presence or inventory records materially increases audit and AML risk and may jeopardize tax-treaty pass-through treatment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated: approximately 25% probability of an unannounced CSSF or AML inspection within the first 18 months of operation for an e-commerce consignment merchant. The likelihood rises to 40% if structured deposits, high-value cross-border luxury shipments, or digital payment rails (Stripe/Escrow Pay) show unusual volumes or counterparty patterns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi coordonnée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales); Articles 944-1 et seq. governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and related provisions applicable to commercial partnerships
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), accessible via the RCSL eDesk portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statutory partnership deed (acte de société) constituting the SCSp, executed either by notarial deed or by private writing, filed with RCSL within one month of signature and subsequently published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; partners freely determine the partnership fund through contributions in cash or in kind; no escrow or blocked-account requirement is imposed by Luxembourg corporate law, although a fiduciary or secured account may be used for e-commerce customer funds at commercial discretion
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: In conformity with the Partnership Deed of the SCSp, the sole general partner hereby resolves as follows: (1) the partnership interests subscribed by the initial partners, together with all contributions declared in Contribution Schedule A, are accepted; (2) the registered office is fixed at 12 Rue de l'Étoile, L-2687 Luxembourg, with power to relocate by manager resolution; (3) the appointment of [Name] as Managing Directeur and [Name] as AML Compliance Officer is ratified; (4) each officer, severally, is authorized to complete RCSL registration, open payment and escrow accounts, and execute all ancillary statutory filings. This resolution is effective immediately. Adopted by the general partner on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute SCSp Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External Luxembourg counsel or notary; alternatively the partners directly, as private writing is permitted for a non-fund SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and finalize the partnership deed in Luxembourgish, French, or English. The deed must identify the specific SCSp name, a genuine registered office in Luxembourg, the general partner (a legal entity or natural person), the limited partner(s), the agreed partnership capital, contribution schedules, profit and loss allocation, management powers, and limitation-of-liability provisions. The general partner and limited partners execute the deed; where a partner is a non-EU entity, signature authentication or apostille must be obtained. The deed must be dated and recorded before all partners receive a fully executed copy.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or EU national identity card of each partner
Proof of residential address for natural persons or registered office for corporate partners
Certificate of good standing or registration excerpt for corporate partners
Final draft of the SCSp partnership deed
AML/source-of-funds declaration for the initial contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is rejected or queried by the registry or notary due to incomplete information, rectify the affected articles and re-execute the deed; if an apostille is unsatisfactory, obtain a supplementary legalized signature within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Luxembourg Bank and Escrow Account and Arrange Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or licensed EMI/PSP; a dedicated escrow service may be used for customer funds in online resale
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a corporate onboarding application at a Luxembourg bank or licensed payment institution, submitting the executed partnership deed, RCSL draft or registration receipt, proof of registered office, UBO declaration, and AML/KYC forms. Transfer the agreed capital contribution into the SCSp's account. If the e-commerce business will hold customer funds, a segregated escrow account must be opened with the bank or an approved escrow service.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate account application
Signed SCSp partnership deed
Passports and proof of address of signatories and general partner
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional substance or compliance evidence, provide the lease agreement, VAT registration or RCSL excerpt, and a detailed payment-flow governance framework; resubmit the enhanced KYC pack within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) eDesk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the RCSL eDesk portal and complete the electronic registration request for an SCSp. Upload the executed partnership deed (notarial or private), consent of the general partner to act as manager, proof of registered office, and valid identification documents. Pay the applicable RCSL filing fee online by card or bank transfer. Obtain the provisional RCSL registration receipt and the Luxembourg legal entity identification number.
required_dossiers: RCSL eDesk registration form
Executed partnership deed
Consent letter of the general partner/managing manager
Copy of a valid passport for each authorized officer
Power of attorney if a local representative files in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL rejects a filing for formal incompleteness, correct the identified fields or upload supplemental annexes through the eDesk ticket system; the statutory one-month deadline is suspended pending full compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish in Luxembourg Official Electronic Gazette and Obtain RCSL Excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES) administered through Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCSL accepts the registration, it automatically triggers publication of the deed and statutory notices in the RES. Verify publication on res.lu, then order the official RCSL excerpt (certificat d'inscription) from the RCSL. The excerpt confirms the SCSp's registration, legal existence, and liability structure, and will be required for tax, banking, and transactional counterparts.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration reference number
Accepted partnership deed
Confirmation of RES publication
Payment receipt for RES publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES publication is delayed or absent after RCSL acceptance, request expedition through the RCSL eSupport help desk and meanwhile obtain a temporary certificate of inscription for all official dealings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Luxembourg Tax ID, VAT and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), accessible via myguichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online registration through myguichet.lu to obtain the corporate tax matricule and Luxembourg VAT number. Indicate the e-commerce resale of second-hand luxury goods and any use of the EU OSS scheme for cross-border distance sales. If the SCSp intends to hire employees, register as an employer with the CCSS and obtain a payer identification number. Review direct tax pass-through treatment with the direct tax administration for the SCSp filing position.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration excerpt or matricule certificate
SCSp partnership deed
Passport or national ID of the manager
Description of the e-commerce business and inventory handling
UBO register extract from the Luxembourg business register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority requests additional economic substance or VAT context, submit the registered office lease, bank account statements, and a concise business description; request a corrected VAT number within 10 days or file for late registration relief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Office, Fire Safety and Municipal Administrative Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg municipal authorities, fire and rescue inspection services, and Ministry of Labour structural/workplace authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office is lawfully used as an administrative or commercial premises under the local municipal development plan. Apply for a fire safety certificate for the office, inspect fire extinguishers and emergency routes, and obtain an electrical installation conformity certificate. If the SCSp later operates a small local stockroom for consigned luxury goods, obtain the municipal occupancy permit and, if applicable, a low-flammability storage authorization. No industrial or environmental permit is needed while the activity remains pure e-commerce re-commerce without processing or manufacturing.
required_dossiers: Office lease agreement or occupancy authorization
Fire extinguisher inspection certificate
Electrical installation conformity certificate
Municipal occupancy permit application
Inventory storage declaration (if local stock is maintained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire brigade or municipality requires supplementary measures, schedule a corrective visit, install the requested equipment (extinguishers, exit signs, emergency lighting), and resubmit the inspection report for clearance within 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the SCSp operates as an e-commerce consignment and second-hand luxury reseller without manufacturing, processing, or an industrial operating site
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for the core activity; a municipal occupancy permit may be recommended if the SCSp later maintains a small stockroom in Luxembourg

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial installation, no significant pollutant emissions, no EIA screening required for online resale of vintage luxury goods
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste streams are generated from administrative office use; if a logistics depot is subsequently operated, compliance with the Luxembourg Law of 9 April 2018 on waste management and with municipal rainwater discharge rules becomes mandatory

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the registered office, compliance with Luxembourg fire-prevention regulations (extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detectors), building structural load inspection if storage is introduced, and workplace occupational safety/health clearance under Ministry of Labour rules

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – VAT and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – direct taxes; electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu / eCDF portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first be inscribed with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS/LBR) to obtain a business registration number ('numéro d'immatriculation'). For VAT, the taxable person files the registration request with the AEDT through the 'eCDF' e-filing platform (form 'Formulaire 2015 – Déclaration de début d'activité' or the dedicated non-established taxable person registration). The AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits, with check code) without any registration threshold for non-established operators. Direct tax TIN for non-resident partners is the 'matricule' assigned by the ACD for withholding/assessment purposes. The representative procedure: foreign entities without EU establishment may be required to appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative for registration if they are not established in the EU, subject to AEDT approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: SCSp (Société en commandite spéciale / Special LP) is fiscally transparent (Pass-Through_Eligible) by statutory default: no corporate income tax, no Luxembourg net wealth tax, no municipal business tax at entity level (unless the SCSp is treated as carrying on a commercial activity for municipal business tax purposes). Income is allocated to and taxed at partner level. Although transparent for direct tax, the SCSp is a distinct VAT person and will be VAT registered in its own name. Cross-border partners: transparency applies only if the partnership classification is recognized in the partner's jurisdiction; otherwise hybrid mismatches arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election. The SCSp's transparency is statutory and non-elective for income/wealth tax (no domestic opacity election for SCSp). Limited alignment elections are available under the ATAD/hybrid-mismatch rules: a taxpayer may apply the OECD nexus approach to align the tax treatment of the transparent entity with the classification in the investor's jurisdiction, and may elect to treat the SCSp as a 'fiscally transparent entity' under Article 2(1)(m) LIR for treaty-look-through. An additional statutory 'option' exists for a Luxembourg partnership to request to be treated as taxable for municipal business tax purposes if it conducts a commercial business (no comparable domestic election for CIT).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) pursuant to the Luxembourg VAT Code (loi du 12 février 1979) implementing Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for established small businesses (franchise regime under Art. 57 VAT Code). For non-established/non-resident taxable persons there is NO registration threshold: VAT registration is mandatory immediately upon the first taxable transaction performed in Luxembourg (distance-selling exemption EUR 10,000 intra-Community applies under the OSS regime, EU-wide, not as a Luxembourg registration threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no SdI/CTC (continuous transaction controls), no digital stamping or API-based clearance in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is legally valid (equal to paper under Art. 10 QR / Directive 2014/55/EU); the Government supports Peppol BIS infrastructure voluntarily and since 2021 mandates Peppol only for receiving invoices from Central Government suppliers (not for traders). VAT compliance is report-based: e-filed periodic returns, EC Sales Lists and Intrastat declarations via the eCDF portal; there is no live API tax clearance obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated when physically exported from the EU by the seller or by the customer (non-established) outside the EU, provided the goods leave the EU within the EU legal deadline (3 months from supply date under Art. 146(j) Directive 2006/112/EC; in Luxembourg within the period documented by CMR/B/L/Customs stamp, generally verified). Conditions: transfer of the right to dispose of goods to the customer, proof of dispatch/transport outside of the EU, and export declaration accepted by Customs (Art. 54 VAT Code). Intra-Community supply to a VAT-registered EU customer also 0% if the customer's VAT number is quoted and EC Sales List filed. Services: B2B services to a non-established customer fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place of supply = customer jurisdiction), and B2C services are taxable in Luxembourg only when effectively enjoyed there; qualifying cross-border services related to goods (export handling, logistics) may be zero-rated. Margin scheme (Art. 57 VAT Code) applies to the sale of second-hand/vintage luxury goods, so VAT is chargeable only on the margin, not on the full selling price; when goods are exported, zero rating applies to the margin.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD – Single Administrative Document / ECS procedure record exported from Luxembourg or country of exit)
Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (for sea freight), Air Waybill (air), CMR consignment note (road), or railway consignment note
Commercial invoice / proforma and purchase contract identifying the buyer, description and export destination
Bank payment evidence / Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing settlement of the export invoice (Stripe/Escrow settlement records)
Proof of physical exit from the EU: customs stamp/ICS/ARN (Movement Reference Number) or ECS confirmation with exit acceptance
Packing list, insurance certificate, and cross-border courier manifest for e-commerce consignments
Any customs warehousing or temporary export documentation if applicable

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent authority for banking prudential supervision and anti-money-laundering compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a euro-area member state, imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. The euro is fully convertible; profit remittances, dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds are freely transferable abroad after satisfying applicable corporate law formalities and tax reporting obligations. No central bank approval is required for cross-border transfers, although EU sanctions regimes, freeze orders, and CSSF AML/CFT reporting obligations must be observed. The absence of capital controls and the full application of EU capital-movement freedom make the Luxembourg SCSp a highly efficient treasury vehicle for inbound and outbound flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg maintains no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratios or timelines for foreign currency receipts. Exporters and e-commerce operators may retain all receipts in foreign currency accounts with Luxembourg credit institutions. Cross-border transactions are subject only to the BCL's statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations under EU/ECB data collection rules, requiring accurate purpose coding and record retention, but not the sale or repatriation of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Escrow Sub-Account for E-Commerce Settlements
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account for Cross-Border Trade

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Domestic Clearing and SEPA Direct Debit Integration
Operational Account for Low-to-Medium Transaction Volumes and SME Treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions operating under the EU passport. An EEA-based EMI registered with the CSSF or passported into Luxembourg can open settlement accounts and provide payment services to the SCSp, provided it holds appropriate safeguarding accounts with a credit institution. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot take deposits or grant credit; their activities are limited to payment transactions, e-money issuance, and remittances. They must comply with CSSF AML/CFT rules and the EU Payment Services Directive. For escrow and luxury resale flows, an EMI combined with a commercial bank account offers operational efficiency without replacing bank-held treasury buffers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory rule requires physical board appearance. CSSF AML regulations permit digital/remote client identification using video verification and qualified electronic signatures. However, given the Medium-Risk_Enhanced classification of online consignment luxury resale, most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks will require at least one senior partner or manager to attend a live video interview and, for the initial onboarding, a physical meeting at the bank's premises may be requested. Beneficial owners and signatories must provide certified copies of passports, proof of residence, and corporate authorization documents; notarized or apostilled versions are commonly mandated for non-EU persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth for high-value vintage luxury inventory and cross-border e-commerce revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Five-year business plan with projected and actual transaction volumes; audited or reviewed financial statements; customer invoices and purchase orders; supplier contracts; customs declarations; luxury goods provenance certificates; bank statements of the funding partner; Luxembourg RCS extract; and a written explanation of inventory sourcing and resale margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of a non-resident-led SCSp with multiple limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement and private placement memorandum; complete ownership chain chart through each natural person beneficial owner; passport copies with apostille; recent bank references from home jurisdictions; CSSF declaration of beneficial ownership (RBE) filed with Luxembourg Business Registers; and signed AML declarations from all partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterfeit or intellectual-property infringement concerns in luxury resale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Brand authentication certificates from independent authentication houses; detailed product provenance dossiers; supplier agreements and official purchase receipts from authorized distributors; eBay/Grailed/Vestiaire Collective or similarly recognized marketplace sales histories; a documented authentication and quality-control process; and cease-and-desist defense evidence if any prior IP dispute existed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers involving higher-risk jurisdictions for settlement of resale proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial contracts and invoices; proof of goods delivery with tracking and customs records; customer identification and sanctions-screening results; bank reference letters; a formal group AML policy with transaction monitoring procedures; and evidence of the SCSp's compliance with EU sanctions, including consolidated EU sanctions list screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and capital injections to the SCSp must be routed through a licensed Luxembourg credit institution or an EEA-authorized EMI. For direct equity subscription, use SWIFT MT103/MT202 wires with the beneficiary being the SCSp's bank account and the remitter stated as the investing legal entity or individual. The wire reference should include the purpose code under the ECB/BOP reporting framework: for direct investment, use the EU Balance of Payments code for 'Direct investment – equity capital' (category F2/F6 or equivalent). Mandatory verification documents include the capital commitment letter, notarized subscription document, partnership agreement extract, anti-money-laundering source-of-funds evidence, and proof of economic substance in Luxembourg if required. For escrow payouts from marketplaces, funds should be routed to a designated virtual account or settlement sub-account with clear remittance information linking to the corresponding sale transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements from the SCSp to overseas luxury suppliers or consignment sellers are executed by SWIFT MT103 for amounts below bank-specific thresholds and where documentary checks are limited. Larger and higher-risk purchase transactions should be supported by an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by a Luxembourg or EU bank, transmitted via SWIFT MT700, and settled against presentation of compliant shipping, insurance, and commercial invoice documents. For continuous e-commerce payouts, the SCSp may use the payment rails of licensed EMIs or the bank's host-host API, with same-day settlement in euros and SWIFT or SEPA-based beneficiary payments. Reconciliations must match invoices, order IDs, and foreign-currency conversion records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts with bank credit line support
Deliverable EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF forwards for market-cleared settlement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted Asian and emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD, EUR and GBP, and EUR and CHF
Plain-vanilla OTC FX options, subject to ISDA master documentation and EMIR clearing eligibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; persistent failure may trigger non-compliance reporting and potential judicial strike-off measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (standard calendar-year deadline: 31 May)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% to 50% of assessed partnership income, plus 0.6% monthly interest; tax authorities may issue official assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing (if statutory audit thresholds are triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; mandatory only if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three size thresholds or has all corporate general partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; loss of audit safe harbor and potential exclusion from public contracts; failure may lead to court-ordered compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average headcount 50; also mandatory where all general partners are legal entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the 1915 Commercial Code; IFRS permitted on a voluntary basis or for consolidated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation must be filed with the RBE within one month of the registration anniversary; any shareholding or partner transfer within the SCSp must be reported to the RBE within one month of the underlying transaction.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate; 17% corporate income tax plus 7% unemployment/solidarity surcharge plus 6.75% municipal business tax; the first tranche of taxable profits below EUR 175,000 may benefit from the reduced 15% CIT bracket)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to online resale of vintage luxury goods. General incentives include the reduced 15% CIT bracket for small taxable income, the 80% exemption under the Luxembourg IP box for qualifying intellectual property income, and the participation exemption for substantial shareholdings. For an SCSp, entity-level tax is generally absent because the partnership is fiscally transparent; the effective burden depends on each partner's tax residence and applicable treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 770 – Luxembourg Annual Corporate Income Tax Declaration (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités); e-filed through the ACD eDesk electronic filing portal accessible via MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (tax year normally aligned with the calendar year; the first accounting period may run up to 12 months and close at the expressly stated commercial year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 May of the following calendar year; the Luxembourg tax administration commonly grants extensions to 31 December. Quarterly instalment payments are normally required during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SCSp's RCS number, 13-digit Luxembourg national registration number, legal name, registered office, legal form code, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are not separately listed unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment or the ACD requests a transparency schedule; attach a schedule of partner identities and residence countries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Tax Status and Treaty Annex
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the entity's legal form as a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and confirm whether an election or administrative determination makes it subject to corporate income tax rather than transparent treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners relying on a double tax treaty should attach a valid Certificate of Tax Residence and any equivalent ACD relief form such as Form 780; if no Luxembourg PE exists, mark no taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Income Allocation and Gross Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross sales from online consignment and second-hand luxury goods retail (ISIC 4791), cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and the partnership net result allocated to the general and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the share of income attributable to a Luxembourg fixed base or permanent establishment is taxable in Luxembourg. Remote e-commerce sales fulfilled and managed outside Luxembourg should be excluded for non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deductible tax losses carried forward within the permitted limit and attach a schedule showing year of origin, amount, and offsetting in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner may offset only losses that are economically attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment; foreign-source losses cannot be claimed on the Luxembourg declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all controlled transactions with associated enterprises, including inventory purchases from related luxury-good suppliers, management fees, loans, and any IP or brand licence fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should separately report cross-border related-party transactions in their home jurisdiction; the Luxembourg entity must support the allocation with transfer pricing documentation where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing may trigger an administrative increase of up to 10% of the tax due, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month capped at 12%, fixed administrative fines where no tax is due, and, in cases of wilful persistent non-compliance, criminal proceedings with fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on Luxembourg-source dividends; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when a 10% qualifying shareholding has been held for 12 months; treaty relief often reduces the rate to 5% or 15%. For a transparent SCSp, periodic distributions are not recharacterised as Luxembourg-source dividends for entity-level WHT, but partners remain taxable in their own jurisdiction of residence)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief the beneficial owner must: (1) confirm treaty entitlement and minimum holding period; (2) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate from its tax authority; (3) submit the TRC and a completed Luxembourg Form 780 or equivalent relief statement to the payer or ACD before the distribution date where possible; (4) for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, provide a parent-company declaration with identity, residence, and equalisation evidence; (5) if tax was withheld at 15%, file a timely refund claim with supporting treaty and beneficial-ownership documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on interest is 0%; domestic withholding tax on royalties is 0%. No source-state tax is imposed on arm's-length interest or licence fees paid to non-residents unless the payment is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment. Certain treaties may preserve a source-country cap of 5-10%, but Luxembourg does not currently impose a statutory royalty or interest WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 (Local File is mandatory when controlled related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 in the fiscal year; a Master File is required when the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the ACD enforces substance requirements through Article 56 LIR, OECD BEPS principles, and the general anti-avoidance rule. The SCSp must demonstrate real activity — premises, employees, strategic decision-making, board records, bank accounts, and commercial risk — in order to preserve pass-through tax treatment, treaty benefits, and the arm's-length character of cross-border transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Conscious Omission in Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate non-declaration of Luxembourg-source profits from online luxury resale, falsification of sales or inventory data, off-shore bank accounts not reported, or destruction of accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of additional tax plus 0.6% monthly default interest, administrative penalty of up to 20% of the deficient tax, forfeiture of hidden assets, and criminal prosecution with court-imposed fines and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or the General Partner can be held jointly and severally liable for tax debts when they knowingly participated in concealment; courts may pierce the corporate veil, imposing civil restitution, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial or Shell SCSp with Insufficient Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SCSp as a brass-plate intermediary to book revenue from vintage luxury sales while all control, staff, inventory, and negotiation functions remain abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg tax residence, denial of treaty benefits, recharacterisation of profits in the partner's residence jurisdiction, application of the GAAR, and an administrative penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted tax; commercial registry dissolution may also be pursued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The General Partner and de facto managers may be personally assessed if the entity is treated as a sham; beneficial partners lose treaty protection, become taxable in their home state, and may be subject to director disqualification and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany purchase of luxury goods at non-arm's-length prices, artificial allocation of profits to a low-tax jurisdiction, absence of a functional and risk analysis, or failure to prepare a Local File once the EUR 250,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary income adjustment plus compensatory interest, ad valorem penalty of 10-20% of the adjustment for deliberate non-compliance, and separate court-ordered fines for incomplete documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation may face personal criminal liability; the tax adjustment may be treated as constructive distribution, exposing officers to civil restitution and cross-border collection measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and KYC Failure in Luxury Resale
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to apply customer due diligence, acceptance of anonymous prepaid cards or laundered funds through payment gateways such as Stripe or EscrowPay, or failure to assess money-laundering risks in the high-value second-hand luxury market.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Luxembourg AML law of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal money-laundering sanctions under the Luxembourg Criminal Code may reach ten years' imprisonment for aggravating circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers, compliance officers, directors, and beneficial owners can be personally fined and imprisoned; authorities may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and professional disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Statutory Tax Return or Transfer Pricing Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the annual Luxembourg tax return, failure to respond to an ACD reminder, or intentional omission of the transfer pricing declaration when the related-party transaction threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the tax payable, monthly interest of 0.6% capped at 12%, fixed administrative fines when the return shows nil liability, and criminal sanction for persistent refusal to file after formal notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the General Partner of an SCSp is the legal representative, it may be held personally liable for filing penalties; persistent non-compliance can result in personal fines, contempt sanctions, and prison time for the responsible individuals.
